import pandas as pd

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source6_98_0 and Source6_98_2 on "Id"
join_0_2 = pd.merge(source0, source2, on="Id", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Operation 2: JOIN Source6_98_1 and Source6_98_3 on "Id"
join_1_3 = pd.merge(source1, source3, on="Id", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Operation 3: JOIN Source6_98_4 and Source6_98_5 on "Id"
join_4_5 = pd.merge(source4, source5, on="Id", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Operation 4: JOIN Source6_98_6 and Source6_98_1 on "Id"
join_6_1 = pd.merge(source6, source1, on="Id", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Now we have four joined DataFrames:
# join_0_2 with columns: Id, SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y
# join_1_3 with columns: Id, SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y
# join_4_5 with columns: Id, SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y
# join_6_1 with columns: Id, SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y

# Next step is to group by Source6_98_0.Id (which is the same as join_0_2.Id)
# and aggregate averages of SalePrice columns from all source tables:
# avg(Source6_98_0.SalePrice) -> join_0_2.SalePrice_x
# avg(Source6_98_1.SalePrice) -> join_1_3.SalePrice_x and join_6_1.SalePrice_y (both from Source6_98_1)
# avg(Source6_98_2.SalePrice) -> join_0_2.SalePrice_y
# avg(Source6_98_3.SalePrice) -> join_1_3.SalePrice_y
# avg(Source6_98_4.SalePrice) -> join_4_5.SalePrice_x
# avg(Source6_98_5.SalePrice) -> join_4_5.SalePrice_y
# avg(Source6_98_6.SalePrice) -> join_6_1.SalePrice_x

# To combine all these, we need to join these four joined DataFrames on Id.

# Join join_0_2 and join_1_3 on Id
temp1 = pd.merge(join_0_2, join_1_3, on="Id", suffixes=('_0_2', '_1_3'))

# Join temp1 and join_4_5 on Id
temp2 = pd.merge(temp1, join_4_5, on="Id")

# Join temp2 and join_6_1 on Id
all_joined = pd.merge(temp2, join_6_1, on="Id", suffixes=('', '_6_1'))

# Now all_joined columns:
# Id
# SalePrice_x_0_2 (Source6_98_0)
# SalePrice_y_0_2 (Source6_98_2)
# SalePrice_x_1_3 (Source6_98_1)
# SalePrice_y_1_3 (Source6_98_3)
# SalePrice_x (Source6_98_4)
# SalePrice_y (Source6_98_5)
# SalePrice_x_6_1 (Source6_98_6)
# SalePrice_y_6_1 (Source6_98_1)

# We have two columns from Source6_98_1: SalePrice_x_1_3 and SalePrice_y_6_1
# We need to average these two for Source6_98_1

# Calculate average SalePrice for Source6_98_1
all_joined['SalePrice_1_avg'] = all_joined[['SalePrice_x_1_3', 'SalePrice_y_6_1']].mean(axis=1)

# Now prepare the final DataFrame with columns as per target schema:
# ['Id': integer,
#  'SalePrice_x': float,          <- Source6_98_0.SalePrice (SalePrice_x_0_2)
#  'SalePrice_y': float,          <- Source6_98_1.SalePrice (average of two columns)
#  'SalePrice_x_3': float,        <- Source6_98_2.SalePrice (SalePrice_y_0_2)
#  'SalePrice_y_4': float,        <- Source6_98_3.SalePrice (SalePrice_y_1_3)
#  'SalePrice_x_5': float,        <- Source6_98_4.SalePrice (SalePrice_x)
#  'SalePrice_y_6': float,        <- Source6_98_5.SalePrice (SalePrice_y)
#  'SalePrice': float]            <- Source6_98_6.SalePrice (SalePrice_x_6_1)

target_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Id': all_joined['Id'],
    'SalePrice_x': all_joined['SalePrice_x_0_2'],
    'SalePrice_y': all_joined['SalePrice_1_avg'],
    'SalePrice_x_3': all_joined['SalePrice_y_0_2'],
    'SalePrice_y_4': all_joined['SalePrice_y_1_3'],
    'SalePrice_x_5': all_joined['SalePrice_x'],
    'SalePrice_y_6': all_joined['SalePrice_y'],
    'SalePrice': all_joined['SalePrice_x_6_1']
})

# Group by Id and aggregate averages as per the operation history
# Although after the joins, Id should be unique, we still follow the instruction to group and average

final_result = target_df.groupby('Id', as_index=False).agg({
    'SalePrice_x': 'mean',
    'SalePrice_y': 'mean',
    'SalePrice_x_3': 'mean',
    'SalePrice_y_4': 'mean',
    'SalePrice_x_5': 'mean',
    'SalePrice_y_6': 'mean',
    'SalePrice': 'mean'
})

# Write the result to the specified path
final_result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

# Read all source CSVs with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
s0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
s1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
s2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

s4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
s5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
s6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Rename SalePrice columns to match target schema suffixes
s0 = s0.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_x"})
s1 = s1.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_y"})
s2 = s2.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_x_3"})
s3 = s3.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_y_4"})
s4 = s4.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_x_5"})
s5 = s5.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_y_6"})
s6 = s6.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice"})

# Join pairs first
join_0_2 = pd.merge(s0, s2, on="Id", how="inner")
join_1_3 = pd.merge(s1, s3, on="Id", how="inner")
join_4_5 = pd.merge(s4, s5, on="Id", how="inner")

# Join s6 with join_1_3
join_6_1_3 = pd.merge(s6, join_1_3, on="Id", how="inner")

# Join join_0_2 with join_4_5
join_0_2_4_5 = pd.merge(join_0_2, join_4_5, on="Id", how="inner")

# Join the two big joins
final_join = pd.merge(join_0_2_4_5, join_6_1_3, on="Id", how="inner")

# Group by Id and aggregate by average on all SalePrice columns to ensure uniqueness and correct row count
result = final_join.groupby("Id", as_index=False).agg({
    "SalePrice_x": "mean",
    "SalePrice_y": "mean",
    "SalePrice_x_3": "mean",
    "SalePrice_y_4": "mean",
    "SalePrice_x_5": "mean",

})
